text:
Logan Stanley is back from a lower-body injury, and the Islanders need his minutes more than usual. He got hurt in the Nov. 14 win in Anaheim (he played 9:24 that night), missed two games, and returned in Detroit on Nov. 21, slotting in beside Matthew Schaefer with Ryan Pulock injured, as Stefen Rosner reported for The Hockey News. On Monday against Toronto he played 24:30.

The scoresheet is bare: no goals, five assists in 21 games, and nothing in his last 11. Our numbers call that drought due, since the chances with him on the ice are up (10.2 on-ice expected goals over his last ten, against 9.3 usual). Offense was never the job, though, for a defenseman with 13 shots all season, even one whose slap shot NHL Edge clocks among the hardest in the league.

His value is elsewhere: 38 blocks, 33 hits, and 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, about five points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season in Winnipeg, so that five-on-five number is the one to keep testing as his minutes climb.
